mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher wage growth, both of which drive upward pressure on S&P 500 valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Payrolls growth does not correlate with SPX 20-day returns (Spearman's rho < 0.2) after controlling for CPIAUCSL and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed within one month by a rebound above the prior quarter's level signals a turning point in supply constraints, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by > 10% in a month then rises above prior quarter GDPC1 in the following month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX 5-day forward window after such GDPC1 pattern (t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) shows a double-digit monthly increase after two consecutive months of contraction, it indicates accelerating demand recovery that reduces production bottlenecks and supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 12% in month 3 after two prior months of < -5% increases
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain flat or negative during such INDPRO pattern (rolling mean p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS below 2% and 4% respectively for three consecutive months create a dual signal of deflationary pressure and policy easing, jointly pushing S&P 500 60-day forward returns higher.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 and FEDFUNDS < 4.0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX 60-day window when both triggers are met (F-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for four consecutive months is interpreted as a labor market cooling that reduces growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% and remains above for four months
failure_condition: UNRATE above 4% is not associated with negative SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in the observable list, so skip) — instead, use HOUST (household spending index) exceeds prior quarter average by 8% in the current month following two months of flat growth, it suggests renewed demand momentum that lifts S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 8% in current month after two flat months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 5-day SPX return after such HOUST pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the monthly index of manufacturing activity (GDPC1) of over 15% for three months indicates deepening supply-side weakness that, if uncorrected, tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by > 15% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative return in SPX 20-day window during such GDPC1 decline (p > 0.05).
